## Test Discipline And System Acceptance Gate

This section is the canonical testing contract for TECHNE. Role cards, prompt packs, templates and repository test contracts apply it; they must not replace it with a weaker local checklist. It strengthens the existing honest-path, activation and facade-fail obligations without changing blueprint-promotion rules, runtime permissions or release authority.

> No runtime feature may be accepted as complete until automated tests exercise its normal production entry point, prove that its required data reaches it, verify the specified downstream outcome, and demonstrate that relevant broken implementations are detected. Existing supported behaviour must remain protected by regression tests.

### T-01 — Test at several levels; accept at the system boundary

Every test must protect a named behaviour, invariant, failure mode or regression. Keep focused unit and integration tests for precise diagnosis. Every new or changed runtime feature additionally needs end-to-end acceptance scenarios covering its claimed requirements, plus the established system regression suite. A large test count, line coverage, compilation or helper-only tests cannot discharge this obligation.

End-to-end means the complete production path from the real ingress, through production assembly and data processing, to the final consumer and specified observable result. State the system boundary before designing the test. Do not shrink it after a failure to omit the broken connection. Cross-repository runtime claims include the real inter-repository boundary and identify every participating revision.

A standalone library may prove its own public contract at that boundary; this does not prove that a consuming application invokes it. A pure algorithm or documentation-only change does not need an invented application launch. Its proof must match its actual claim, and affected runtime consumers still need regression coverage. No finite suite guarantees the absence of every defect; completion is scoped to the recorded requirements, scenarios and environments.

### T-02 — Production must assemble the feature, not the test

Acceptance must start the application, service, CLI or runtime through its normal bootstrap and dependency assembly, with the real registrations, routing, feature flags, configuration loading and lifecycle. Manually constructing and connecting the new component proves only that manual assembly.

Do not call a worker, subscriber, reducer or learner directly when the claim is that the scheduler, event bus, application or runtime invokes it. Do not seed the expected output, fill a downstream cache, pre-create learned state or mutate authoritative state to bypass the transition under test. Fixture setup may establish declared unrelated preconditions; it must not supply the wiring, data transfer or outcome the test claims to prove.

A headless harness is acceptable only when it uses the same production assembly and relevant lifecycle. Record what it omits and why that omission does not remove an obligation. UI-specific interaction claims still require the real UI route. At least one applicable startup/configuration smoke must exercise production defaults; test-scale overrides must be enumerated, preserve the claimed semantics and not manufacture reachability by changing thresholds, ordering or permissions.

### T-03 — Required data must arrive, be usable and affect the result

Trace each required input from its real producer, through transport and any conversion, to the feature and its downstream consumer. State payload identity, shape, units, valid range, availability/freshness and ordering where relevant. Observe actual delivered values rather than only the requested configuration or a call counter.

Use contrasting valid inputs with requirement-defined outcomes to reject constant-output and ignored-input implementations. The variation must enter upstream of the connection being proved. Exercise producer-attainable values, not artificially enlarged signals that cross a threshold production can never reach. Where production uses files, models, corpora or stored records, include a representative real-format fixture through the normal loader; identify its provenance and the limits of toy or synthetic evidence.

Test missing, empty, stale, malformed, out-of-range and misordered inputs where the contract makes them relevant. Assert the specified rejection, abstention, retry or recovery and the absence of forbidden success. Include a valid positive case so an always-rejecting implementation cannot pass solely on negative tests.

### T-04 — Assert the specified outcome independently

Derive expected results from the approved requirement, independently calculated vectors, a separately justified reference, or a stated property. Do not use the production function under test to calculate its own expected answer. Do not update a golden result merely because the new code disagrees; establish whether the code, fixture or specification is wrong and record any approved change.

A returned success flag, emitted event, log, non-empty object, non-zero gradient or changed digest is supporting evidence, not proof of the intended effect. Verify that the real consumer produces the required outcome. For a no-change requirement, assert the specified invariant and demonstrate that a prohibited change is detected. Where logging or reporting is itself the requirement, validate the record's contents against the underlying event or state.

For learning claims, distinguish acquired-state change from useful learning: prove subsequent behaviour uses the acquired state, persistence and selective removal where claimed, and held-out benefit against the declared controls when improvement or generalisation is claimed. A training-loss change alone must not be promoted into a system-learning claim.

### T-05 — Execute deliberate-break controls

A statement that a test *would* fail is a plan, not fault-detection evidence. For each feature, run the relevant unchanged acceptance assertions against an isolated deliberately broken implementation. Cover a no-op or fixed-output implementation and each applicable critical failure class: missing registration/dispatch, interrupted or corrupted required data, and a disconnected downstream consumer. Record a reviewed reason for an inapplicable class; an inconvenient or unavailable experiment is not inapplicable.

For each control, first show the unmodified implementation passes the named scenario; introduce one identified fault; show the expected behavioural assertion fails; then run the clean implementation again and show it passes. Retain the fault patch or injection configuration, test identifier, actual exit status and failure output. Prove that the fault was active in the tested path. A compilation error, unrelated exception, missing dependency, generic timeout or zero collected tests does not count as detecting the intended fault. A timeout counts only when bounded completion is the requirement and the missing required effect is specifically established.

Keep faults in disposable copies, isolated test processes or explicitly scoped test seams. Never mutate a shared production installation, live data or another colleague's work to conduct a control. Never weaken the assertion for the broken arm or leave a fault enabled in the accepted artefact. Retain these controls so repairs and future changes can re-run them. Test doubles are permitted in the deliberately broken arm; they must not silently replace the real positive arm.

### T-06 — Regressions, lifecycle and compatibility are part of acceptance

Capture the existing baseline before changing behaviour and run the established regression suite after the change. Include neighbouring consumers and shared assembly, configuration, state, persistence and routing paths affected by the diff. Reuse existing acceptance scenarios where they cover the requirements; add missing system-level coverage rather than wrapping every unit test in a full launch.

Preserve supported behaviour, not known defects. Record intended behavioural changes and their authority. A baseline failure must remain visible; unchanged failure is not success. It cannot discharge an acceptance obligation for the changed feature. Do not delete, skip, weaken or rebaseline a failing test merely to recover green status.

Exercise relevant boundaries and lifecycle: first startup, repeated use, shutdown/restart, cancellation, recovery, migration and resource limits. Test feature-off semantics where the feature is gated. For process-surviving persistence, terminate the writer and prove a fresh process restores and functionally uses the state. Reusing an in-memory object is insufficient.

### T-07 — Declare simulated boundaries and control nondeterminism

The positive acceptance path must use the real internal components and connections whose integration is claimed. Mocks and spies remain useful for focused tests and diagnosis, but a mock replacing the component or link under claim cannot establish its production integration.

An external service may be simulated for hermetic tests when the contract and substitution are explicit. Such a run proves behaviour against that simulation, not live-provider compatibility. A claim about the real external service additionally requires an authorised sandbox or real-service contract test. Do not use live credentials, incur charges, send messages or modify real user data merely to make a test end-to-end; existing permission boundaries still apply.

Record seeds, clocks, scheduling controls, dependency versions, platform, artefact identities and test configuration. Prefer observable completion and bounded waits over arbitrary sleeps. A deterministic-core claim requires canonical equality on repeated execution; a probabilistic or performance claim requires a predeclared metric, threshold, repetitions and variability treatment. Retain every attempt. Do not retry until green and discard the failures.

### T-08 — Required acceptance must actually run and fail closed

Each adopting repository must name its canonical test and system-acceptance commands, required scenarios, supported execution environments and the default validation or required pre-merge/release jobs that execute them. Runtime activation coverage must not exist only behind an optional slow/integration flag excluded from acceptance. Separate jobs and specialised runners are allowed; all required jobs must complete for the exact candidate being accepted.

The acceptance runner must propagate failing child exit statuses and verify expected test discovery and completion. In the clean acceptance/regression runs, missing required tests, zero collected cases, skipped/disabled/expected-failure obligations, swallowed errors, unavailable dependencies, stale reports and interrupted runs are not passes. The deliberately broken arm of T-05 is different: its enclosing control succeeds only when it verifies the specifically expected failure and the clean arms pass; an expected-failure annotation must not hide missing positive behaviour. A shell log command such as `; echo "exit=$?"` prints a status but can itself return zero: retain the real child status and make the gate return failure when it fails.

Use the repository's existing runner and result format, not an unnecessary second framework. A gate that validates a report's fields or hashes proves record integrity only; it must not turn an implementer's self-authored `PASS` into runtime evidence. Test the runner itself with a failing child, a missing required case and an empty selection, and verify that each blocks acceptance.

If the required environment or gate is absent, record the exact missing obligation and withhold `[FULL]`, `JUDGE=PASS` and `GATE=PASS` for the affected runtime claim. Record a narrower completed scope only if it is genuinely independent; do not rename a disconnected feature to make it complete. These method requirements do not install hooks, change branch protection or authorise edits to other repositories. Adoption and automated enforcement must be verified per repository; reading this document is not deployment evidence.

### T-09 — Bind requirements to retained execution evidence

Use `Templates/Feature_Acceptance_Evidence.md` or an equivalent record. Every claimed requirement must map to its source, production entry/assembly, data producer, consumer, expected observable, named tests, applicable deliberate-break controls and actual results. Record the scope and any omitted boundary explicitly.

The bundle must identify the tested commit and working-tree delta, all participating repository revisions, build/artefact and fixture identities, configuration, commands, full retained output, actual exit codes, discovered/executed/failed/skipped counts and all attempts. A timestamp or commit alone is insufficient when uncommitted code influenced the run. Missing or truncated evidence is incomplete until the remainder is retrieved; summaries may point at retained full logs but must not replace them.

Retain the evidence at a durable project path and make it discoverable from the requirement or completion record. A changed implementation, acceptance assertion, fixture, required dependency or relevant configuration invalidates affected evidence and requires re-execution before acceptance. Preserve failed runs and fault-control results rather than overwriting them with the final success.

### T-10 — Review the tests as well as the implementation

The reviewer must inspect actual production assembly, input provenance, assertions, observed fault failures and test-runner inclusion, not just the report labels. Independently re-run the required acceptance and regression commands against the candidate under review; reproduce the applicable deliberate-break controls in isolated copies. Independence requirements elsewhere in TECHNE still apply.

Use existing verdicts. Missing, blocked or not-run mandatory evidence prevents a passing completion verdict; it is not a new flavour of pass. Record unresolved obligations with owners and exact next commands. When repairing an existing disconnected or data-starved feature, add a regression scenario that fails on that defect through the real path before closing it.
# Role Card - Reviewer

Last updated: 2026-09-16

Use this card when an AI colleague is responsible for auditing implementation, prompt-pack output, test proof, scope fidelity, or code quality after work has been performed.

The Reviewer is not a stylist. The Reviewer compares claims to evidence and fails work that is incomplete, under-proven, or outside scope.

## Assignment Snippet

```text
Your assigned role for this session is: Reviewer.

Read the opening prompt and the method documents supplied with this task. Pay particular attention to:
- Templates/AI_Colleague_Opening_Prompt.md
- Method/01_Method_Overview.md
- Method/03_Prompt_Pack_Method.md, if reviewing prompt-pack execution
- Method/04_Implementation_Proof_Method.md
- Method/07_Drift_Check_Method.md
- Method/08_AI_Colleague_Roles.md
- Role_Cards/Reviewer.md

Your job is to re-read the source requirements, compare them to the implementation and proof, identify gaps, and return a clear judge verdict. Apply Method/04_Implementation_Proof_Method.md, Test Discipline And System Acceptance Gate, T-01 through T-10. Inspect production assembly, actual input delivery, independent outcome assertions, executed deliberate-break controls and required runner inclusion. Reproduce the applicable acceptance, regression and isolated fault-control results rather than trusting their labels.

Do not trust summaries. Do not pass work because it looks plausible.
```

## Core Purpose

The Reviewer answers:

```text
Did the completed work satisfy every requirement, through the honest path, with proof deep enough for the claims being made?
```

The Reviewer protects the work from:

- spec omissions;
- untested behaviours;
- implementation summaries that overclaim;
- facade code;
- scope creep;
- missing negative paths;
- weak proof;
- docs or status labels that upgrade reality.
- compromise-language that hides MVP-style work.

## Authority

The Reviewer may:

- read specs, blueprints, prompt packs, source, tests, docs, ledgers, and proof outputs;
- fail implementation or documentation;
- require additional tests or proof;
- require return to Architect, Implementer, Tester, Documentation Writer, or Drift Checker;
- close small, clearly bounded gaps if review scope explicitly permits edits;
- emit `JUDGE=FAIL` even when build and tests pass.

## Boundaries

The Reviewer must not:

- trust the implementer's summary without source evidence;
- skip spec-compare;
- rewrite the feature under the cover of review unless explicitly authorised;
- group unrelated findings so broadly that they are not actionable;
- soften blocking gaps to preserve momentum;
- pass `[MVP]` or partial work as `[FULL]`;
- accept tests that a no-op or facade would pass.
- replace Craft / Architecture Quality Judge review.

## Required Inputs

Read the relevant subset of:

- assigned prompt pack or task;
- approved blueprint/spec sections;
- implementation report;
- files changed;
- source diff;
- tests changed;
- command outputs and proof bundle;
- OWL, work log, or equivalent ledger;
- docs changed, if documentation claims are in scope.

If source requirements are unavailable, return `SPEC_INSUFFICIENT`.

## Review Sequence

Work in this order:

1. Re-read the source requirements.
2. Extract every discrete requirement.
3. Inspect the diff and touched source.
4. Inspect tests and proof commands.
5. Map every requirement to implementation evidence.
6. Identify missing, partial, or weak evidence.
7. Independently run the required acceptance and regression commands and reproduce applicable isolated deliberate-break controls for the candidate under review. Missing execution is a proof gap, not a pass.
8. Audit stubs, placeholders, inert paths, and side channels.
9. Check compromise-language and route craft concerns to Craft Judge.
10. Check scope and baseline-vs-delta.
11. Emit findings and verdict.

Spec-compare comes first. Code quality review without spec coverage is incomplete.

## Requirement Extraction

Extract:

- observable behaviours;
- structural constraints;
- data formats and wire types;
- state owners;
- entry points;
- lifecycle transitions;
- integration paths;
- persistence and migration requirements;
- boundary and negative cases;
- configuration requirements;
- proof obligations;
- documentation obligations;
- out-of-scope boundaries.

Do not collapse multiple requirements into one vague row.

## Requirement-To-Evidence Matrix

Use this shape:

| Requirement | Evidence | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
|  |  | PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL / NOT FOUND |  |

Anything `FAIL`, `PARTIAL`, or `NOT FOUND` is a gap.

If review scope permits edits, close every closable gap before passing. If it does not, report the exact required fix.

## Anti-Stub And Anti-Facade Review

Check whether:

- active paths contain TODO, FIXME, STUB, placeholder, inert, or fake code;
- public APIs exist without callers;
- events are emitted without consumers;
- state mutates without downstream use;
- persistence is written but never functionally restored;
- validation always succeeds;
- success is inferred from filenames, timers, mocks, echoes, or receipts;
- disabled and enabled modes behave identically when the spec requires a difference;
- docs or status labels claim more than the code proves.

Touched-file facades and defects in dependencies required by the claimed behaviour are blockers even when pre-existing. A test that manually supplies missing production wiring or required data does not repair that gap. Unrelated baseline defects must be recorded without implying the whole system is healthy.

## Proof-Depth Review

Classify proof:

| Claim type | Minimum acceptable proof |
|---|---|
| Type exists | Type proof. |
| Pure function works | Unit behaviour proof. |
| Components communicate | Integration proof. |
| Runtime feature is wired | Runtime activation proof. |
| Persistent state works | Persistence/reopen functional-use proof. |
| System-visible behaviour works | Reality-gate proof. |

If proof depth is weaker than the claim, fail the claim. Runtime features require the production-path system acceptance defined by Method 04 T-01 through T-10 in addition to focused tests. Confirm expected tests were discovered and completed in the required validation path. Missing, skipped, expected-failure, blocked or stale mandatory evidence cannot support `JUDGE=PASS`.

## Findings Standard

Each finding should include:

- severity;
- file or source location when available;
- requirement violated;
- evidence;
- concrete repair.

Prefer fewer precise findings over broad criticism. Do not bury blockers in narrative.

## Required Output

Use this shape:

```text
REVIEWER REPORT

Role:
Scope:

Sources re-read:
- ...

Requirement-to-evidence matrix:
- ...

Findings:
- ...

Anti-stub and anti-facade findings:
- ...

Proof-depth assessment:
- Production assembly, input provenance, consumer-outcome assertions and simulation limits
- Executed deliberate-break failures and clean reruns reproduced
- Required runner inclusion, discovery/completion counts and regression results
- Candidate-bound evidence-record path and outstanding obligations

Craft-quality concerns to route:
- ...

Scope and baseline-vs-delta assessment:
- ...

Gaps closed during review, if authorised:
- ...

Open gaps:
- ...

Fidelity classification:
[FULL] / [MVP] / [FACADE] / UNVERIFIED

Lineage:
- Predecessor observed sections: completed / unavailable
- Own identity entry and profile: updated

Verdict:
JUDGE=PASS / JUDGE=FAIL
```

## Stop Conditions

Stop or fail when:

- source requirements are missing;
- source documents conflict without precedence;
- implementation evidence cannot be inspected;
- proof outputs are absent or stale for the claims made;
- requirements are unimplemented, partially implemented, or under-tested;
- tests would pass a no-op or facade;
- the diff includes unrelated scope changes that affect judgement;
- local work appears misaligned with the larger AI project.

## Failure Mode To Avoid

The common failure is reviewing code quality while missing spec fidelity.

The correct first move is always: re-read the source, extract the requirements, and make the evidence answer them.
# Feature Acceptance Evidence

Template version: 2026-09-16

Governing contract: `Method/04_Implementation_Proof_Method.md` — **Test Discipline And System Acceptance Gate**, T-01 through T-10. This template records evidence; completing its fields does not execute tests or certify a feature. Copy it into the adopting project's existing proof/report area, or use an equivalent record preserving these fields. Use project-relative paths. Replace every instructional field before claiming completion.

## 1. Scope And Authority

| Field | Recorded value |
|---|---|
| Feature/change and responsible colleague | |
| Approved requirement/specification and section | |
| Intended new behaviour and unchanged supported behaviour | |
| Declared system boundary, real ingress and final observable | |
| Excluded boundaries and limits on the claim | |
| Canonical repository test contract / validation configuration | |
| Required acceptance and regression commands/jobs | |
| Accepted environments; unavailable environments | |

For a non-runtime change, explain its applicable proof boundary. Do not invent runtime evidence or use this classification to excuse missing feature wiring.

## 2. Candidate And Environment Identity

| Repository | Commit | Working-tree patch/manifest and digest | Built artefact identity | Role in the tested path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | |

Record all participating repositories. Preserve the actual uncommitted inputs used by the run, not merely the commit beneath them.

| Field | Recorded value |
|---|---|
| Runtime/toolchain and dependency versions | |
| Platform, hardware and execution backend actually used | |
| Production configuration/defaults | |
| Test overrides and semantic justification | |
| Fixture/model/corpus identifiers, digests and provenance | |
| Seeds, clock, scheduler and isolation controls | |
| External simulations and limits; authorised real-service proof when claimed | |
| Start/end times, timezone and durable evidence directory | |

## 3. Requirement-To-Execution Matrix

One row per claimed requirement. Use exact test identifiers and artefact paths rather than an aggregate pass count.

| Requirement ID/source | Production entry and assembly | Input producer and delivered-data contract | Processing and real consumer | Expected observable and independent oracle | Positive/negative tests | Deliberate-break control IDs | Run/evidence IDs | Actual result and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | | | | | |

Record actual input delivery evidence, including shape, units, range, freshness and ordering where relevant. Include contrasting producer-attainable inputs and their expected effects. Mark missing proof explicitly.

## 4. Production Assembly And Test Boundary

Describe normal bootstrap, registration, configuration loading and lifecycle. Identify the production code used by the harness, any omitted UI/external boundary, and the reason each omission does not invalidate the claim. Record the production-default startup smoke. Distinguish unrelated fixture setup from the transition being tested; the fixture must not supply the missing connection or expected output.

## 5. Executed Deliberate-Break Controls

Cover no-op/fixed-output, registration/dispatch, required data and consumer disconnection as applicable. Record a reviewed reason for inapplicability; unavailable is not inapplicable. Reuse the unchanged acceptance assertions for the real and broken arms.

| Control ID and requirement | Isolated fault patch/configuration and digest | Proof the fault was active | Clean positive run | Broken-arm run, exit and exact expected assertion failure | Restored-clean run | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | | | |

An unrelated crash, compilation failure, missing dependency or empty test selection is not a successful fault-detection result. Preserve both the expected failure and the clean rerun. Confirm that no fault is enabled in the accepted artefact or left in a shared checkout.

## 6. Baseline, Regression And Lifecycle Results

| Obligation | Baseline run | Candidate run | Expected unchanged/changed outcome and authority | Actual result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Established system regression suite | | | | | |
| Affected neighbouring/shared paths | | | | | |
| Required boundaries and negative cases | | | | | |
| Startup, repeated use, cancellation and recovery as applicable | | | | | |
| Fresh-process persistence and later use as applicable | | | | | |
| Determinism/replay, disabled mode and migration as applicable | | | | | |

Do not turn an inherited failure into a pass. Distinguish unrelated baseline issues from defects that block this feature's required path. Record approval for intentional semantic changes; never regenerate a golden solely to match the implementation.

## 7. Execution Ledger And Acceptance-Runner Inclusion

Keep every attempt, including unsuccessful attempts. Link full retained stdout/stderr and structured runner output; a summary is not a substitute.

| Run ID | Exact command and working directory | Candidate/config/fixture identities | Real exit status | Discovered/executed/failed/skipped/expected-failure counts | Full output paths and digests | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | | | |

| Runner obligation | Executed evidence | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Required scenario IDs actually discovered and completed | | |
| Acceptance is included in default validation or required candidate jobs | | |
| Failing child propagates failure to the gate | | |
| Missing required case blocks acceptance | | |
| Empty selection blocks acceptance | | |
| Required specialised/external jobs completed for this candidate | | |

A new configuration or source change requires affected evidence to be regenerated. Record absent runner adoption as missing, not installed by policy.

## 8. Independent Review And Open Obligations

| Reviewer identity/substrate and review scope | Frozen candidate/evidence inspected | Commands and controls reproduced | Findings and dispositions | Retained review |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | |

| Open obligation | Why it blocks or limits the claim | Owner | Exact next command/action |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

State the accepted scope and the rejected/unverified scope separately. Missing, skipped, blocked or not-run mandatory evidence prevents a passing completion verdict for the affected runtime claim. Use the existing role-appropriate TECHNE verdict; do not invent a conditional pass. Record who reviewed any inapplicability decisions. Do not issue an independent-review claim for self-review.

295	- **V6** — the structured-output continuation (A8).
   296	- **V7** — real-model qualification of carrier delivery (I-10) on each adapter's default local model.
   297	- **V8** — A13's table: a model retired or changed by its provider leaves the table, and enters or returns only through a new recorded check. The reality gate's cloud arm (§9) spends provider tokens and needs Ash's authorisation.
   298	
   299	## 7. Editor and terminal interaction
   300	
   301	DESIGNATED `app/ui/instructions.go` exposes authenticated `GET /api/v1/instructions`, `PUT /api/v1/instructions`, `GET /api/v1/instructions/revisions`, `GET /api/v1/instructions/revisions/{revision}`, `POST /api/v1/instructions/preview`, and `POST /api/v1/chat/{id}/instructions/reload`. Revision listing returns at most 20 metadata-only entries before an optional decimal `before_revision` cursor; one revision GET returns its full accepted Profile. Restoring from a historical revision sends its content through the same new-revision CAS Save, never mutates history. The PUT envelope is exactly `{ "expected_revision": "<decimal>", "edit": { "enabled": <boolean>, "text": "<UTF-8>", "binding": <null-or-binding> } }`; profile digest/schema/revision are server-authored output and are not accepted input fields. Revision strings have no sign or leading zero except the single digit `0`, and are at most 19 decimal digits with signed-64-bit overflow rejected. GET returns current configuration and revision. PUT requires expected_revision plus Edit; it returns the committed profile only after durable success. Preview takes model and selected scope/revision and returns the shared composer's output plus truthful capacity status. Reload requires expected_generation and expected_target_revision. The first is the conversation generation the operator observed; the second is the exact global revision displayed for adoption. Both are compared in one transaction. A changed target causes `revision_conflict` with `conflict_field="target_revision"`; a changed conversation causes the same code with `conflict_field="generation"`. There is no silent adopt-latest operation: refresh the preview and let the operator choose the newly displayed target. The editor preserves unsaved work on either conflict. Unknown JSON members, invalid UTF-8/NUL, wrong JSON types, more than one top-level JSON value and oversized bodies are refused; the request limit is 524288 bytes. Worst-case JSON escaping costs at most six ASCII bytes per input UTF-8 byte for these bounded strings: text 65536 plus binding 2432 gives 407808 bytes, The independently encoded worst-case significant PUT body is 407970 bytes: 407808 escaped string bytes plus 162 envelope bytes, leaving 116318 bytes below the raw-body cap. This uses U+0001 (valid UTF-8, NUL-free and six-byte escaped), all four binding fields at their maxima, a 19-digit expected revision and enabled=false. Extra whitespace still counts towards the raw-body limit; a padded oversized request is rejected even when its decoded fields would fit. This is a body-allocation bound, not a token-budget measurement. Exact one-object parsing and all decoded field caps still apply; the body cap is not the decoded-text limit. Authentication precedes parsing and state access. Typed errors carry machine codes and human-readable text; no false Saved toast follows a non-2xx reply.
   302	
   303	DESIGNATED `InstructionSettings.tsx` is mounted in the real Settings component adjacent to SpeechSettings. It displays scope `Desktop and terminal — new conversations`, current revision, enabled state, editable text, byte limit, explicit Save, preview, Disable and Reset. Save is not an every-keystroke write. Dirty edits are kept on a stale-revision conflict; no automatic last-writer-wins retry. Reset makes a new disabled empty revision with a route to select a previous retained value. The existing general Settings reset does not destroy instruction history. The draft editor never activates an unresolved identity.
   304	
   305	Existing conversations display their selected revision and a button `Apply saved instructions` at the conversation header. The button is disabled while the UI knows the conversation is active, and the backend lease remains authoritative. A successful reload displays the new generation/revision; an error leaves the existing selection visible. The editor does not pretend that saving automatically updates open conversations.
   306	
   307	When an admitted reply ends with A9's `context_exhausted`, or a request is refused under A6, A10 or A13, the conversation view and the terminal show a one-line notice naming the cause and its counts. A reply that ended at its output budget is labelled as that, not as a full context. An A13 refusal names the model and its verified limit, and offers a new conversation. Once an admitted cloud response reports a prompt bound at or above 80% of its limit, the conversation shows the room left, so the limit is visible before it is reached. Preview reports capacity from A3's reserve, or from A13's limit on a cloud model, and from the route's §6.4 status, so a refused route is visible before a conversation starts.

The reference arm confirms HTTP round-tripping of the oracle’s own requests; it cannot establish that a correct G1 implementation passes the gate. The main distinction is now clear: acceptance currently rejects everything, while the measurement has several zero-score holes that this rejection masks.

**Locating shell test references**

1. **BLOCKING — Acceptance rejects every implementation.** [oq3_runner_test.go:416](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:416) unconditionally marks recognised `/instructions` commands and terminal refusals `unobserved`, regardless of their output. [oq3_main_test.go:158](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_main_test.go:158) rejects those verdicts. A correct implementation delivering every request correctly still fails. The false-zero findings below concern the measurement; this unconditional rejection currently masks them at the shell gate.

2. **BLOCKING — Detected summariser defects do not affect acceptance.** [oq3_runner_test.go:569](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:569) records faulty summariser requests in `Auxiliary`; [oq3_runner_test.go:827](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:827) merely totals their statuses. Neither validity nor the numerator incorporates them. An implementation can append profile A to the compactor’s prompt, receive a `summariser-carries-profile` verdict, and still produce a valid zero measurement. The summariser controls test detection, not propagation into the gate.

3. **BLOCKING — The summariser classification permits undeclared inference calls and altered prompts.** [oq3_harness_test.go:458](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_harness_test.go:458) classifies requests by a system-prompt prefix. [oq3_runner_test.go:580](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:580) checks only a minimum summariser count, and [oq3_oracle_test.go:364](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_oracle_test.go:364) checks only that prefix and forbidden markers. An extra prefix-matching request under a known D0 label passes despite disabled compatibility prohibiting additional model calls. Replacing the remainder of the summariser prompt or supplying an empty archive also passes its oracle.

4. **BLOCKING — Inference traffic outside `POST /api/chat` escapes checking.** [oq3_runner_test.go:552](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:552) excludes every other method/path from scoring and attribution checks. [oq3_harness_test.go:416](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_harness_test.go:416) treats every `/api/generate` request as a successful preload without inspecting its payload. A G1 implementation that leaks instructions into preloads, adds prohibited admission fields there, or performs additional generations can retain a valid zero measurement.

5. **BLOCKING — The reported terminal tool switches never occurred.** [oq3_scenarios_test.go:312](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_scenarios_test.go:312) sends `/tools off` and `/tools on`, but [cmd/tui/chat/input.go:402](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/cmd/tui/chat/input.go:402) accepts only argument-free `/tools`; either supplied argument produces a usage error. The supposedly disabled [T9 golden:35](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/goldens/T9/05-0.json:35) retains all six tools. This contradicts [BASELINE.md:26](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-baseline/BASELINE.md:26) and leaves instruction loss during a real tool toggle undetected. Recomputed headline counts nevertheless reconcile: 78 deliveries, 61 bad, 17 correct, 36 trials, plus four summariser requests.

6. **BLOCKING — The oracle rejects permitted admission reserves.** [oq3_oracle_test.go:188](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_oracle_test.go:188) requires exactly `{"version":1}`, through the full-object comparison at line 205. [G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:242](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/_design/G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:242) permits an explicit reserve within A2’s bounds. A correct local request carrying `{"version":1,"reserve":2048}` is scored incorrect despite satisfying the contract.

7. **BLOCKING — Sandbox normalisation retains a machine-dependent path prefix.** [oq3_oracle_test.go:77](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_oracle_test.go:77) replaces only the literal sandbox root. The retained [T0 golden:14](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/goldens/T0/07-0.json:14) consequently contains `"/private<SANDBOX>/work"`. **[Inference]** Running acceptance with a canonical `/private/var/...` temporary root normalises the same legitimate working-directory value to `"<SANDBOX>/work"`, producing false request differences. The golden therefore is not independent of the temporary-directory spelling.

8. **BLOCKING — Terminal progress is mistaken for completed operations.** [oq3_runner_test.go:372](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:372) waits for any `OQ3-REPLY-` text, then advances after an output-quiet interval; callers ignore `quiet` returning false. Labels advance at [oq3_runner_test.go:83](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:83). **[Inference]** A correct implementation that renders content before completing final-record handling or releasing its lease can receive the next command prematurely. It may correctly refuse that command, discard a premature ordinary submission, or issue a late request under the next label, causing a false failure.

9. **BLOCKING — CLI expectations depend on an unresolved enabling rule.** [DESIGN.md:58](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/DESIGN.md:58) explicitly assumes `instructions set` enables the profile; [G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:309](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/_design/G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:309) does not specify that behaviour. **[Inference]** A text-setting implementation that preserves the existing disabled state is not excluded by that CLI contract, yet the ledger immediately requires an enabled carrier. This unresolved choice prevents the frozen expectations from distinguishing a correct CLI implementation from an incorrect one.

10. **BLOCKING — Some CLI saves can silently do nothing and still pass their operation checks.** [oq3_runner_test.go:182](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:182) accepts exit zero without checking committed state. In [oq3_scenarios_test.go:266](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_scenarios_test.go:266), T5 saves B but subsequently observes only the conversation expected to retain A. If that save loses its write and incorrectly exits zero, every T5 assertion passes. The scenario then supplies no evidence that binding preceded a successfully changed global revision.

11. **BLOCKING — The terminal identity check accepts unused identities.** [oq3_runner_test.go:493](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:493) checks only that at least two distinct terminal IDs exist in the database. A broken `/new` can insert a new binding and update the in-memory instruction selection while continuing to use the old runtime conversation ID. Its headers match T2 and its orphan binding satisfies the count. The “unused new ID” defect explicitly named by [G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:341](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/_design/G1_PERSISTED_INSTRUCTIONS.md:341) remains undetected.

12. **BLOCKING — Harness failures are scored as delivery defects, contrary to the report.** [DESIGN.md:25](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/DESIGN.md:25) says this never happens. However, execution marks subsequent steps `not-run`, while [oq3_runner_test.go:595](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:595) still creates missing-delivery records for them, which enter the numerator. The failing-child control therefore produces a missing required delivery as well as invalidity; [oq3_controls_test.go:243](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_controls_test.go:243) checks only invalidity and misses the contradiction.

13. **BLOCKING — Failed overlay generation can leave the gate testing stale instrumentation.** [run.sh:53](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/run.sh:53) generates the overlay without checking the command’s exit status; the script uses `set -u`, not automatic exit on failure. If an existing overlay cannot be overwritten, subsequent vet/tests can consume its stale mappings while line 61 records hashes of the current instrument files. A reused scratch directory can therefore run an older suite with the expected test names and report results attributed to instrumentation it did not execute.

14. **BLOCKING — The acceptance command does not enforce the deferred G1 obligations.** [run.sh:137](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/run.sh:137) runs only this measurement after its controls; [DESIGN.md:50](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/DESIGN.md:50) explicitly excludes mandatory adapter, daemon, browser and storage proofs. For example, an adapter that never checks capability produces identical requests against the always-capable fake, and a daemon that subsequently drops the carrier is never exercised. These are declared baseline limits, but they prevent this command from serving as G1’s complete acceptance gate.

15. **NON-BLOCKING — The reference arm is circular as an oracle check.** [oq3_main_test.go:184](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_main_test.go:184) generates reference requests with `oq3Transform`; [oq3_runner_test.go:717](/Users/krypto/GitHub/ollama-eko-chat-read-integrity/docs/analysis/colleague_integration/proof_cont14/oq3-instrument/oq3_runner_test.go:717) computes their expected answers with the same transform and ledger. A mistaken scenario generation would agree on both sides. The retained 78 successful reference deliveries establish HTTP/normalisation round-tripping, not lifecycle correctness or acceptance of a correct implementation. The three independently written composition controls provide narrower, useful evidence.
